header.title: Flex
header.description: Declarative flexbox: arrange children in a row or column with `direction`, `align`, `justify`, `gap` and `wrap`, without writing CSS by hand. Use it for toolbars, stacks and action groups. If you need columns aligned across rows, use `Grid` or `Row` and `Col`.

playground.title: Playground
playground.description: Tweak the props and see the result and the code instantly. The frame has a minimum height so `justify` in a column and `align` in a row are visible; item 2 is taller.

toolbar.title: Toolbar
toolbar.description: `justify="between"` sends the title to the start and the actions to the end; `align="center"` centers them vertically. The actions are another Flex with a smaller `gap`. The examples use this item and these demo styles.

direction.title: Direction
direction.description: `direction` sets the main axis: `row` (default) lays out horizontally and `column` vertically. The `-reverse` variants only flip the visual order; screen readers and keyboard focus follow the source order.

stack.title: Vertical stack
stack.description: With `direction="column"` and `align="stretch"`, each child takes the full width. It is the simplest way to stack a label, a control and helper text with even spacing.

gap.title: Spacing
gap.description: Unlike Grid, Flex has no default spacing: without `gap` it is 0. It accepts a spacing token (`3` is `var(--gem-space-3)`), any other number (treated as pixels) or any CSS length. With `wrap`, `rowGap` separates the lines and `columnGap` the items on the same line.

wrap.title: Wrapping
wrap.description: By default children stay on a single line and shrink or overflow. `wrap` moves them to the next line when they don't fit, and `wrap="wrap-reverse"` stacks the lines from bottom to top. Resize the window to see the difference.

justify.title: Justify
justify.description: `justify` distributes leftover space along the main axis (`justify-content`). `between` keeps the ends against the edges, `around` adds half a gap at the edges and `evenly` uses the same space everywhere. In flexbox, `stretch` behaves like `start`: to make a child grow, use `flex-1`.

align.title: Align
align.description: `align` aligns children on the cross axis (`align-items`). Without `align`, they stretch to the tallest one (`stretch`). `baseline` aligns the first line of text even when font sizes differ.

alignContent.title: Align content
alignContent.description: `alignContent` only has an effect with `wrap` and when the container is taller than its lines: it distributes that space between the lines (`align-content`). Don't confuse it with `align`, which aligns items within each line.

grow.title: Flexible children
grow.description: Flex controls the container; each child's size is set with classes on the child. `flex-1` makes it take the free space, `ms-auto` pushes it to the end and `shrink-0` prevents it from shrinking. For long text to be truncated with an ellipsis, the flexible child needs `min-w-0`.
grow.longText: A long text that doesn't fit in the available space is truncated with an ellipsis instead of pushing the rest.

inline.title: Inline
inline.description: `inline` uses `display: inline-flex`, so the Flex flows inside text instead of taking its own line. Since `as` doesn't accept `span`, the Flex renders as a `div`: the surrounding text must be a `div`, not a `p`, for the HTML to be valid.

texts.after: and we'll let you know when it ships.

centered.title: Centered
centered.description: `direction="column"` with `justify="center"` and `align="center"` centers content on both axes. Useful for empty states or loading screens; the container needs a height for vertical centering to show.

texts.title: No projects yet
texts.body: Create the first one to get started.

withRow.title: Flex with Row
withRow.description: Flex and Grid work together: Flex builds the header row (title and actions, with `wrap` for narrow screens) and `Row` with `Col` splits the content into columns. The Grid page explains the CSS that per-breakpoint spans need.

header.title: Flex API
header.description: API reference for the Flex React component: props, CSS classes, CSS variables, tokens and exported types.

demos.title: Demos
demos.description: For examples and usage details, visit the component demos page.

import.title: Import
import.description: Import it from the main entry or from its subpath to load only the layout.

inheritance.title: Inheritance
inheritance.body: Accepts HTML attributes (HTMLAttributes<HTMLElement>) and passes them to the root element. ref reaches the element. gap, rowGap and columnGap become CSS variables inside style, merged with the style you pass.

a11y.title: Accessibility
a11y.order: With row-reverse, column-reverse or wrap-reverse only the visual order changes. If order matters, change it in the source.
a11y.landmark: With as you can render nav, header, footer or aside instead of a <div>.
a11y.list: For a group of links or tags, use as="ul" and <li> on each child so the number of items is announced.
a11y.label: If a bar groups related controls, give it role="toolbar" or role="group" and a name with aria-label.

cssClasses.title: CSS classes
cssClasses.description: Classes you can use to override styles.

cssVariables.title: CSS variables
cssVariables.description: `.gem-flex` sets `--gem-flex-gap: 0`. If you don't pass `gap`, you can redefine it from a class; if you do, it is written inline and can only be overridden with `!important`.

items.--gem-flex-gap: Space between children. Set by `gap`; defaults to 0.
items.--gem-flex-row-gap: Space between lines with `wrap`. Set by `rowGap`.
items.--gem-flex-column-gap: Space between children on the same line. Set by `columnGap`.

items.--gem-space-{n}: Spacing scale used by `gap`, `rowGap` and `columnGap` when they receive a token.

types.title: Exported types
types.description: Available from @gem-org/gem-system to type your own wrappers. Flex shares its types file with Grid, Row and Col.

props.title: Props
props.description: Also accepts the root element's HTML attributes.

items.direction: Main axis. The `-reverse` variants flip the visual order.
items.wrap: Moves children to another line when they don't fit. `true` equals `"wrap"`.
items.gap: Space between children: spacing token, pixels or CSS length.
items.rowGap: Space between lines. Takes precedence over `gap`.
items.columnGap: Space between children on a line. Takes precedence over `gap`.
items.justify: Distribution of leftover space on the main axis (`justify-content`).
items.alignContent: Distribution of space between lines with `wrap` (`align-content`).
items.inline: Uses `display: inline-flex` to flow inside text.
items.className: Extra classes for the root element.
items.classNames: Per-slot classes. `root` is added to the root element.
items.style: Inline styles. Merged with the gap CSS variables.
